text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT - Inference GPU queue > 10k for redwood-prod. Spot worker pool experiencing concurrent preemptions; autoscaler failing to provision fallbacks. Paging @jamie oncall (primary).
jamie: seeing the alert — I’m pulling logs now. queue growth started ~ 4m ago. preempt counts spiking on spot pool us-west-2-gpu-spot.
sasha: oncall-bot shows "scale_rejected: reached max_deployment_limit" for dedicated-pool-1. Might be quota cap hitting the reserved pool.
jeam (typo)leo: tagging in — I can jump to infra console and check quota. @maria can you confirm any customer-facing incidents reported yet?
maria: CS flags: two customers reported higher 5xx rates and timeouts on streaming responses. CS ticket IDs: CS-8471, CS-8472. They said timeouts ~30-45s.
jamie: quick mitigation options: 1) temporarily pull traffic to smaller model variant (gpt-4o-lite) 2) force-evict spot pool and route to reserved 3) increase autoscaler max (if quota allows). Which do we want first?
sasha: I think forced routing to reserved first. If reserved is at capacity maybe fallback to CPU quantized workers for lower throughput but reduce 5xx.
leo: checking reserved pool usage... `reserved-gpu-pool` at 92% baseline, but there are some free nodes in dedicated-pool-2 across regions. Autoscaler rejected because `max_pool_instances` set to 80 and we've reached it.
ops-bot: infra event: API call `scale.modify` by jamie (session id 9f2c) failed: quotaExceeded. Error: "Per-project GPU quota exceeded: requested 8 > allowed 2".
jamie: damn. quota constraints. Can we request emergency quota bump? That takes time. Alternative: spin up additional reserved instances in eu-central where quota available and route a subset of traffic there.
maria: CS: start proactive notifications for impacted customers: say we're mitigating and expect reduced errors in 15-25m. Also offer to failover particular critical keys to priority routing.
sasha: plan: (A) enable model-level degradation for non-critical routes to `gpt-4o-quant` (int8), (B) update routing policy to prefer dedicated across regions where quota exists, (C) temporarily disable spot-only pools to stop churn.
jamie: executing step C now: disabling spot pool autoscaling and scaling spot worker group to 0 to stop further preemptions. `infractl workergroup scale spot-usw2-gpu 0 --reason "incident 1759347200"`
ops-bot: `infractl` response: job queued (id b3c4). Estimated completion 60s.
leo: while that runs, I'm patching the routing policy to route 30% of traffic to eu-central reserved and 70% to remaining us-west dedicated. Patch command:
```
routectl update-service redwood-inference --split 30:70 --targets eu-central:reserved, us-west:dedicated
```

ops-bot: route update applied. New traffic split active in ~45s.
jamie: applying model degradation for non-SLAs: `deployctl override-model default:generation gpt-4o-quant --scope non-sla`
ops-bot: model override accepted. Non-SLA routes will use quantized variant.
maria: CS: posting updates -> "We observed GPU capacity exhaustion due to spot preemptions chaining with autoscaler limits. We've routed traffic to other regions and applied lower-accuracy fallbacks. Monitoring closely."
eng-manager: good. Also track error budget burn for any customers we escalate. Jamie — can you put timeline + mitigation steps in incident tracker? I'll coordinate with PM.
jamie: adding notes to incident tracker: root cause = concurrent spot preemptions + autoscaler max cap + quota prevents immediate reserved scale-up. Mitigation = disable spot pool, reroute traffic, model fallbacks, request quota bump. Timeline included.
sasha: open action item: autoscaler should not reject when spot losses happen; it should attempt cross-region scale or fallback to CPU workers. Filing a follow-up ticket: ENG-OPS-1293.
leo: quick check — request for emergency quota submitted to cloud provider (ticket 924321). ETA unknown but mentioned expedited escalation. Also enabling soft-fallback to CPU: `deployctl enable-cpu-fallback --service redwood-inference --max-latency 120s`
ops-bot: CPU fallback toggled. Note: throughput will drop; this is to reduce 5xx and avoid timeouts.
jamie: monitoring metrics — queue length peaked at 11.2k, now trending down to 3.7k after route change. p95 latency for streaming dropped from 18s to 7s.
maria: CS: customers responded: CS-8471 says errors reduced but requests still slower. We've offered temporary priority keys and will follow up when resolved.
eng-manager: good job. Next: 1) formal post-incident RCA, 2) policy change to avoid spot-only critical capacity, 3) autoscaler changes (cross-region fallback + emergency-reserved threshold), 4) run a preemption stress test.
sasha: noted. I'll draft the RCA and include repro steps and monitoring playbooks. Assign to ENG-OPS-1293.
jamie: handing off oncall to @sasha for follow-up and postmortem. I'm out for 1hr. Sasha, please continue coordination with CS and infra.
sasha: ack — taking over. I'll keep monitoring and update the incident doc. If queue stops decreasing or reserved pools hit 100% again, escalate to on-call secondary.
oncall-bot: handoff recorded: from jamie -> sasha at 1759347480. Handoff note: mitigations applied; monitor queue and customer impact; escalate if > 5% error rate persists.
leo: final note — add autoscaler test cases to CI: simulate 3x spot preemptions and ensure fallback routes trigger within 60s. I'll create ENG-TEST-445.
maria: CS will follow up with impacted customers with a formal incident summary and temporary credits where appropriate.
jamie: thanks team. I'll sync with PM and ops to request quota increase and schedule the stress test tomorrow.
sasha: closing live mitigation segment. Moving to postmortem thread. :white_check_mark:
